name: Boston University
header:
Boston University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Application is January 11, not the common January 15 date.
• Saving a referee starts an email invitation.
• International fee-waiver request requires substantial draft materials before submission.
• No late document replacement through central admissions.
• Robert Pollack joined Arizona by Fall 2026; BU now lists him as Affiliated Professor, so do not assume ordinary
BU doctoral supervision. The number-theory research page has older personnel entries. Weinstein is on
sabbatical throughout 2026-27. Takashi Kimura’s recent publication/project availability needs direct
confirmation.
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.
• No original paper newer than the 2017 anchors verified after author, publisher and subject-focused searches.
Unrelated Japanese physicists and medical researchers share this name.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A mathematics or closely related bachelor's degree meets the stated academic entry qualification. UChicago
math therefore satisfies degree-type eligibility if completed before enrollment; admission remains selective.
[s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Use a permanent email and full legal name. Choose only one GRS program; cannot simultaneously apply to a
GRS MA and PhD. Start references early. Request any departmental international fee waiver before paying. [s1]
[s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Admissions/program queries: mathdept@math.bu.edu. Public application list does not require prior supervisor
agreement. Faculty list below is a research shortlist, not confirmed availability. [s1] [s12]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use BU GRS Liaison application linked from s1. Reference FAQ and document FAQs provide public mechanics;
portal was not entered and no referee invitation was sent. [s1] [s3]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Current admissions page explicitly identifies Fall 2027 and Mathematics Jan 11. Funding dollar rate for that
cohort remains unverified. [s1]

Academic application [2027 confirmed]
January 11, 2027, 11:59 pm Boston / Eastern time. [s1]

Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
No separate entrant fellowship deadline found; submit complete PhD application by January 11, 2027. [s1] [s9]
Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
January 11, 2027. Letters must reach the portal by the application deadline even if the applicant submits
earlier. [s1] [s3]

offer-specific date unconfirmed. The page labels Eastern UTC-05 even though April normally observes daylight
time; follow Boston local time and ask if an offset is specified. [s10]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
English proficiency required; routes include citizenship, U.S. bachelor's degree, qualifying English-medium
degree/study, or tests. If testing: TOEFL 5.0 (tests from Jan 21 2026) or old-scale 100; IELTS Academic 7;
Cambridge 185; Duolingo 130. [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Yes: received or expected U.S. bachelor's before program start satisfies the rule. Indicate that degree in the
application; no additional action is stated for this route. [s5]
GRE General [Unresolved]
Not listed among Mathematics PhD Fall 2027 required materials. Public math entry does not specify whether
submitted scores are considered; confirm optional-score handling. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
Not listed among Mathematics PhD Fall 2027 required materials. Do not transplant Statistics' recommendation
to Mathematics; confirm current math-specific submission policy. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [2027 confirmed]
Three academic references. Use writers in the proposed field who know your work. [s1] [s3]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No extra entrance-fellowship letter established. Later GRAF/GRUF funding requires an adviser letter and
separate proposal; not a pre-admission requirement. [s9]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Saving an online recommendation automatically emails the writer. Use professional institutional email;
personal Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo addresses are not accepted. [s3]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations and submissions can occur before applicant submission; recommenders can submit afterward, but
still before the deadline. [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Portal checklist shows received/pending items; recommender page allows reminder emails. [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Only the application system is accepted; no Interfolio, email, fax, or mailed letters. Replacing an already
submitted letter or reusing a prior-cycle letter is not explained publicly. [s3]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume is on the general checklist. Relevant experience; one page typical, two or three may suit substantial
experience. Upload, max 15 MB; accepted formats include PDF/DOC/DOCX/RTF/TXT and common images. [s4]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
BU calls this a Personal Statement: required. Prompt paraphrase: explain qualifications and intended study
objectives clearly. Minimum 200 words; approximately 750 words/two pages typical; upload ceiling 5 pages.
Name and department/degree on every page; English-language document settings. [s4]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
The required Personal Statement is the academic-purpose document above. A separate background essay is
not listed; portal-specific supplements unverified. [s1] [s4]
Research-interest statement [Unresolved]
May be addressed in the required statement; no separate research-interest document is listed in the public
math requirements. Any separate prompt/length/upload slot is unverified. [s1]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
No research proposal is listed in public math application requirements; no format or upload permission
established. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No writing sample is listed for Mathematics in the current program requirements. Extra-paper upload/link policy
unverified. [s1]
Publications list [Unresolved]
Publications may be included in the CV; separate publications-list upload or linked-paper requirement not
established. [s4]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
The public mathematics and graduate-admissions pages checked do not establish a separate requirement or
permission to submit this item. Required/optional status, exact prompt, length, formatting and

upload-versus-link instructions remain unverified; check the current portal before drafting or sending an extra
document. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No entrant fellowship essay publicly specified. Departmental fee-waiver request requires personal statement
and research summary plus CV and transcripts; no length/format for research summary stated. [s6]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Submitted personal statement/CV cannot be replaced through the central office; direct new accomplishments
to the program. [s4]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Living stipend specified in admission offer; a verified 2027-28 math dollar amount was not found. Full
required-course tuition, mandatory services/wellness fees, and basic SHIP premium credit during full-stipend
semesters are described. Do not substitute engineering/CS rates. [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Up to five years from matriculation, subject to conditions and funding availability. [s9]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
New domestic and international PhD students are eligible for fellowship funding. [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Good conduct, good standing and satisfactory progress required; package may combine training, teaching, and
research fellowships. Service assignments generally 20 hours/week; funding availability caveat applies. [s9]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Department funds PhD students through university fellowships, teaching and grants. Offer contains details; no
separate initial funding application found. [s11]
Other funding routes [Prior cycle]
After enrollment, GRAF/GRUF travel-research awards and GSO travel grants exist; these are not entrance
stipend guarantees. GRAF/GRUF require separate proposal and adviser reference; current posted competition
is 2026, not 2027. [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 95, nonrefundable, paid in portal by Visa/MasterCard/AmEx/Discover. [s7]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
International applicants must contact mathdept@math.bu.edu, not central admissions. Include full name,
application email, CV, personal statement, research summary, transcripts. Department decides whether to
recommend waiver. Requests at least 5 business days before deadline; never pay before waiver approved. [s6]

Number theory and arithmetic geometry

Explicit and computational arithmetic geometry: p-adic heights and integration, Chabauty methods and
rational points on curves. [faculty1] [faculty1a]
Professor and Director of Graduate Admissions; new supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · Shadow line distributions
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Jared Weinstein
p-adic geometry, local shtukas, Langlands correspondences and modularity; connections to chromatic
homotopy. [faculty5] [faculty5a]
Professor; on sabbatical Fall 2026 and Spring 2027. Confirm availability for Fall 2027 advising.
Research evidence: 2026 · Higher modularity of elliptic curves over function fields
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.

text:
Boston University
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verification is maintained separately.
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Application is January 11, not the common January 15 date.
• Saving a referee starts an email invitation.
• International fee-waiver request requires substantial draft materials before submission.
• No late document replacement through central admissions.
• Robert Pollack joined Arizona by Fall 2026; BU now lists him as Affiliated Professor, so do not assume ordinary
BU doctoral supervision. The number-theory research page has older personnel entries. Weinstein is on
sabbatical throughout 2026-27. Takashi Kimura’s recent publication/project availability needs direct
confirmation.
• Faculty below form a verified research-fit shortlist, not a complete census. New-student supervision and 2027
leave/moves must be confirmed; paper dates describe the cited version.
• No original paper newer than the 2017 anchors verified after author, publisher and subject-focused searches.
Unrelated Japanese physicists and medical researchers share this name.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
A mathematics or closely related bachelor's degree meets the stated academic entry qualification. UChicago
math therefore satisfies degree-type eligibility if completed before enrollment; admission remains selective.
[s2]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Use a permanent email and full legal name. Choose only one GRS program; cannot simultaneously apply to a
GRS MA and PhD. Start references early. Request any departmental international fee waiver before paying. [s1]
[s6]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
Admissions/program queries: mathdept@math.bu.edu. Public application list does not require prior supervisor
agreement. Faculty list below is a research shortlist, not confirmed availability. [s1] [s12]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use BU GRS Liaison application linked from s1. Reference FAQ and document FAQs provide public mechanics;
portal was not entered and no referee invitation was sent. [s1] [s3]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Current admissions page explicitly identifies Fall 2027 and Mathematics Jan 11. Funding dollar rate for that
cohort remains unverified. [s1]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
January 11, 2027, 11:59 pm Boston / Eastern time. [s1]

Funding consideration [2027 confirmed]
No separate entrant fellowship deadline found; submit complete PhD application by January 11, 2027. [s1] [s9]
Reference receipt [2027 confirmed]
January 11, 2027. Letters must reach the portal by the application deadline even if the applicant submits
earlier. [s1] [s3]
Test-score receipt [2027 confirmed]
Any required English scores must be received for completion by January 11, 2027. UChicago degree route can
satisfy English without testing. GRE handling is not explicit on math's current requirement list. [s1] [s5]
Supporting documents [2027 confirmed]
January 11, 2027: application and supporting credentials must be complete. [s1]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Offer letter controls. General FAQ says most PhD offers expire April 15 at 11:59 pm Boston time; 2027
offer-specific date unconfirmed. The page labels Eastern UTC-05 even though April normally observes daylight
time; follow Boston local time and ask if an offset is specified. [s10]
English and GRE
English requirement [Standing rule]
English proficiency required; routes include citizenship, U.S. bachelor's degree, qualifying English-medium
degree/study, or tests. If testing: TOEFL 5.0 (tests from Jan 21 2026) or old-scale 100; IELTS Academic 7;
Cambridge 185; Duolingo 130. [s5]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Yes: received or expected U.S. bachelor's before program start satisfies the rule. Indicate that degree in the
application; no additional action is stated for this route. [s5]
GRE General [Unresolved]
Not listed among Mathematics PhD Fall 2027 required materials. Public math entry does not specify whether
submitted scores are considered; confirm optional-score handling. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Unresolved]
Not listed among Mathematics PhD Fall 2027 required materials. Do not transplant Statistics' recommendation
to Mathematics; confirm current math-specific submission policy. [s1]
Academic records
Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload legible copies of official or unofficial transcripts in the application. Do not send unsolicited originals,
mail, email, or third-party transcript delivery for application review. Non-English records need translations;
official final records follow admission. [s8]
Mathematics-course list [Unresolved]
The public admissions checklist checked does not establish a separate mathematics course-list requirement.
Confirm any portal-only supplement and its format; omission here does not mean unsolicited uploads are
permitted. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Course descriptions [Unresolved]
The public admissions checklist checked does not establish a separate course-description/textbook-list
requirement. Confirm any portal-only supplement and its format; omission here does not mean unsolicited
uploads are permitted. [s1] [s2] [s3]

Recommendation letters
Number and type [2027 confirmed]
Three academic references. Use writers in the proposed field who know your work. [s1] [s3]
Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No extra entrance-fellowship letter established. Later GRAF/GRUF funding requires an adviser letter and
separate proposal; not a pre-admission requirement. [s9]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Saving an online recommendation automatically emails the writer. Use professional institutional email;
personal Gmail/Outlook/Yahoo addresses are not accepted. [s3]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Invitations and submissions can occur before applicant submission; recommenders can submit afterward, but
still before the deadline. [s3]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Portal checklist shows received/pending items; recommender page allows reminder emails. [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Only the application system is accepted; no Interfolio, email, fax, or mailed letters. Replacing an already
submitted letter or reusing a prior-cycle letter is not explained publicly. [s3]
Written materials
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
CV/resume is on the general checklist. Relevant experience; one page typical, two or three may suit substantial
experience. Upload, max 15 MB; accepted formats include PDF/DOC/DOCX/RTF/TXT and common images. [s4]
Statement of purpose [Standing rule]
BU calls this a Personal Statement: required. Prompt paraphrase: explain qualifications and intended study
objectives clearly. Minimum 200 words; approximately 750 words/two pages typical; upload ceiling 5 pages.
Name and department/degree on every page; English-language document settings. [s4]
Personal / background statement [Unresolved]
The required Personal Statement is the academic-purpose document above. A separate background essay is
not listed; portal-specific supplements unverified. [s1] [s4]
Research-interest statement [Unresolved]
May be addressed in the required statement; no separate research-interest document is listed in the public
math requirements. Any separate prompt/length/upload slot is unverified. [s1]
Research proposal [Unresolved]
No research proposal is listed in public math application requirements; no format or upload permission
established. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Unresolved]
No writing sample is listed for Mathematics in the current program requirements. Extra-paper upload/link policy
unverified. [s1]
Publications list [Unresolved]
Publications may be included in the CV; separate publications-list upload or linked-paper requirement not
established. [s4]
Course-list document [Unresolved]
The public mathematics and graduate-admissions pages checked do not establish a separate requirement or
permission to submit this item. Required/optional status, exact prompt, length, formatting and

upload-versus-link instructions remain unverified; check the current portal before drafting or sending an extra
document. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Scholarship essays [Unresolved]
No entrant fellowship essay publicly specified. Departmental fee-waiver request requires personal statement
and research summary plus CV and transcripts; no length/format for research summary stated. [s6]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
Submitted personal statement/CV cannot be replaced through the central office; direct new accomplishments
to the program. [s4]
Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Living stipend specified in admission offer; a verified 2027-28 math dollar amount was not found. Full
required-course tuition, mandatory services/wellness fees, and basic SHIP premium credit during full-stipend
semesters are described. Do not substitute engineering/CS rates. [s9]
Years of support [Standing rule]
Up to five years from matriculation, subject to conditions and funding availability. [s9]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
New domestic and international PhD students are eligible for fellowship funding. [s9]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Good conduct, good standing and satisfactory progress required; package may combine training, teaching, and
research fellowships. Service assignments generally 20 hours/week; funding availability caveat applies. [s9]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
Department funds PhD students through university fellowships, teaching and grants. Offer contains details; no
separate initial funding application found. [s11]
Other funding routes [Prior cycle]
After enrollment, GRAF/GRUF travel-research awards and GSO travel grants exist; these are not entrance
stipend guarantees. GRAF/GRUF require separate proposal and adviser reference; current posted competition
is 2026, not 2027. [s9]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 95, nonrefundable, paid in portal by Visa/MasterCard/AmEx/Discover. [s7]
Fee waiver [2027 confirmed]
International applicants must contact mathdept@math.bu.edu, not central admissions. Include full name,
application email, CV, personal statement, research summary, transcripts. Department decides whether to
recommend waiver. Requests at least 5 business days before deadline; never pay before waiver approved. [s6]
Conflicts and remaining checks
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
English testing FAQ has generic wording about review-time waivers; dedicated international page supplies
explicit U.S.-bachelor satisfaction route. Use dedicated rule. Commitment FAQ UTC offset is inconsistent with
April daylight time. [s5] [s10]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm Mathematics GRE submission/consideration policy;2027-28 stipend and summer terms; separate
portal supplements/course lists; submitted-letter replacement/reuse; and offer-specific commitment deadline.
